title: Fashion Portfolio
introduction: A selected portfolio of four projects exploring research, form, material, illustration and final fashion outcomes.

projects.title: Mr Blobby The Constructed Man
projects.subtitle: Major Studio 2: Graduate Collection
projects.description: The flâneur, a nineteenth-century figure of urban observation, is reimagined within the contemporary city. No longer a detached spectator, he moves between identities, cultures and spaces; tracing connections through the urban landscape. Inspired by the work of Martine Rose and Wales Bonner, this collection explores hybridity: the intersection of person and place, body and environment. He follows paths to nowhere and everywhere, navigating the overlooked spaces between destinations. Cutting through the route not taken, he binds the fractured seams of the city together. He adorns the weathered posters, layered textures, and splattered murals; he becomes both observer and participant in the evolving urban fabric.

projects.title: Soft Edges, Rough Corners
projects.subtitle: Body Mapping Upcycled Capsule Collection
projects.description: Soft edges rough corners text: Tensions & Intentions pulling, tearing, mending and making; narratives, stories; sentiments of wounded wovens, speaking through torn threads, stains of times passed. reforming, remoulding, reimagining the imagined; intentions eat into new tensions, new tears, new wounds. made new again, new but old, old but new. intention is in the tension; text maps the tensions of the body, mapped now in meanings from times passed, reforming, remoulding, reimagining. A rough and organic reimagining of streetwear aesthetics. Upcycled jersey and denim garments use texture, text and signs of wear as modes of communicating the concept “soft edges, rough corners” a hybrid collection that blurs boundaries between gender, form, the body and the vox populi’s identity.

projects.title: Tumble Forms
projects.subtitle: Body Form Capsule Collection
projects.description: This project explored the direct relationship between the human form, anatomical structure, materials, and garment construction. Moving beyond flat patternmaking, the designer draped, manipulated, pleated, and sculpted fabric directly on the body and dress form, drawing on skills developed in patternmaking and construction, body mapping, and constructed textiles. The result is an experimental capsule of works that tests physical volume, silhouette, and tactile qualities.
